name.description: What people call it: one line of 1 to 100 characters, with no space at either end.

in.description: The id of the system the app is part of, a record in systems/.

only.description: The condition under which the thing is there at all, begun with "when", "on" or "for", so that it reads after the word "only": `only: when a customer pays by card`. One line of at most 100 characters. Left out when it is always there.

description.description: What it is responsible for, in 1 to 2,000 characters. Its first sentence says what the thing is: a box shows that sentence.

kind.description: How the app runs. service: it runs until it is stopped. browser: in a person's browser. mobile: on a phone or a tablet. desktop: a program a person starts on their own machine. command: a person or a script starts it, and it ends. function: started by an event. job: started by a schedule.

technology.description: What it is built with, or the format it keeps: ids of records in technologies/, a set. Never a protocol a part only speaks. When it is built with one of several, name them all and say in the description that one is chosen.

owner.description: The id of the owner, a record in owners/, who answers for the part. Left out, it is that of what the part is in.

source.description: Where its code lies: one to three paths of a file or a folder, counted from the folder that holds the model's folder, written with `/`. A path with `..`, with `*` or with `/` at its start is an error, and the check warns when a path is not there. For a part built elsewhere, the file here that starts or pins it. Left out where nothing of it is at hand.

description: Code that runs as a unit of its own: started, deployed or scaled apart from the rest. One code that a deploy file or config starts under two commands or roles is two apps; copies of one are one app. The subcommands a person types at a program are that program. A part built elsewhere and started or pinned here is an app too. In one system. C4 calls it a container.
